posts.description:
Our annual fashion tech hackathon looked a little different this year, in the best way! This year we welcomed college students across the AUC and partnered with MontAIge (Founder, Mariama Barry) and Spelman Innovation Lab!

This year's theme: AI in Fashion, exploring how AI moves beyond simply generating images or designs. Students explored how an AI pattern generator (MontAIge) and computational fashion technologies can support the creative process, translate design intent into physical production, and help us rethink what fashion can do to address real-world social challenges.

The hackathon was just the beginning. Two finalists teams will now continue their journey to Runway in the Cloud, The Fashion-Tech Soirée on Saturday, December 5, where they will showcase their designs in the Innovation Gallery.
Runway in the Cloud guests will be able to view and judge on the finished garments to cast their vote for viewers’s choice and win a grand prize! Tickets: https://lnkd.in/emMQUVAA #thenextitgirl #runwayinthecloud #fashiontech

Every AI founder I talk to asks me the same question: “Do you know any great FDEs?”

It makes sense. Forward deployed engineers are the ones who actually make AI work inside real companies. They take messy workflows, ship inside enterprises, and a lot of the time they’re the reason a deployment succeeds or doesn’t. Every great AI company wants more of them, and the best ones are being really thoughtful about where they go next.

So we figured, why not get them all in one room?

On Wednesday, November 18, Peri is hosting it's FDE Night, a small, invite-only evening for the best FDEs in the city and the AI teams building alongside them.

Founders and engineering leaders from some of the fastest-growing AI companies will come up two at a time for a quick-fire panel. Short pitches, good questions, straight to the point. We’re keeping the lineup quiet until Monday, November 16, when confirmed guests will get it first. After that, it’s open bar, food, and yes, I’ll be DJ'ing 🎧 

One thing I’m really excited about: everyone gets a company handwritten on the back of their name tag. That’s our pick for who you should meet that night. If it clicks, we’ll make the intro.
We’re keeping it small on purpose. Most of the list is curated, but we’ve saved a few spots and I’ll be personally reviewing every request.

If you’re an FDE at a top startup, a very technical engineer looking to break into the FDE space, or you’re building a team that runs on FDEs, I’d love to see you there: https://luma.com/z7uj8rje

PS: Shoutout to the Peri team who helped put this together! Miles Judd Porter Agatha Advincula Faith Carty Lochlain Healy Bryce James Anthony Lamelas

#FDE #ForwardDeployedEngineering #AI #Startups

posts.description:
I had a great time at the FINOS OSFF conference in NYC last week. A high point for me was the workshop during lunch, where the Scott Logic team held an open session on "Rethinking Software Development for the AI Era". Lots of great collaboration from the ~60 attendees. Key points below:

Challenges
• Trust, validation and human accountability - AI can generate substantial quantities of code, but appropriate review processes that establish trust remain difficult.
• Security, regulation and governance - How can we ensure AI-generated software meets regulatory requirements, and that he development process itself is compliant and auditable?
• Existing delivery processes - in most banks the SDLC limits velocity, for good and bad reasons! The ability to move quickly is increasingly important
• Skills and knowledge - How will job satisfaction be impacted? What skills does the engineer of the future need?
• Organisational commercial challenges - Business stakeholders and rapidly prototype, creating tensions and increased expectations of release velocity.

Opportunities:
• Legacy modernisation and tech debt - AI could significantly reduce the cost and effort of addressing tech debt.
• Faster experimentation - AI lowers the cost of turning ideas into working software
• Improved quality and security - Attendees acknowledged the risk of "AI Slop" but collectively felt this is a technology that, if used correctly, will improve quality
• New approaches to engineering - As AI becomes more capable, many of the processes we have taken for granted will change.

A fascinating conversation. We are at an interesting point, where it is clear that almost everything about how we engineer software is going to change - but how it will change, and what it will become is still quite unclear!

comments.text:
I agree that the pattern is that more science and more socio-technical application leads to “more human flourishing”. The problem today is that our elites and managerial class are actively hostile to our flourishing. 

On the idea that in the recent past “AI was far behind humans at almost every cognitive task”, but “it is on track to surpass us at almost everything we can do intellectually”, perhaps the __relative__ change is as much – or more – that human intellectualism __has regressed__, and that humanity is under-rated?

We so want to deny our abilities, our learning skills, and our agency that we almost wilfully submit to abstracted “non-human” process, to “the machine”. 

These are three ideas that machine learning could not reach.
comments.author: Nico Macdonald

posts.description:
Last week we hosted Richard Socher of Recursive at the GV (Google Ventures) Ferry Building in San Francisco following the launch of Recursive's first model, Flint, and his new book, Eureka Machine.

The conversation ranged from how to budget compute across parallel research branches to whether AI can be as 'stubborn' as required to do the most difficult and non-obvious things.

Beyond the technical debate, Richard pointed out a simple truth: when we were born, AI was far behind humans at almost every cognitive task: language, reasoning, perception. Within our lifetimes, it is on track to surpass us at almost everything we can do intellectually.

Despite this, people are increasingly worried about AI in our future. Richard’s counter is simple: the future needs better marketing.

If you ask someone how AI changed their life this week, the answer usually feels incremental. But historically, the progression has always held true:

More science → more technology → more economic growth → more human flourishing.

That chain of progress is the reason billions of people can live on this planet today. With AI, the clock speed is tightening.

You can see that acceleration in Recursive's recent launch of Flint. A small team used their automated research system—the Eureka Machine—to build a frontier-class model from scratch in under four months, automating the entire pipeline from tokenizer to post-training.

When Richard and I first discussed recursive self-improvement eighteen months ago, it was a deeply contrarian take. Today, it is reality. When the machine starts building the machine, we are no longer playing a zero-sum game. In fields like life sciences, we are just rapidly expanding the pie.

Huge thanks to Richard and the brilliant room of AI researchers and founders from Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Mistral, Reflection AI, and UC Berkeley that attended. 

Eureka Machine book on Amazon - https://lnkd.in/etG6YQZ9

posts.description:
Thrilled to welcome 6 new PS Fellows to PostScriptum: a Nobelist & ex-Skype, MySQL, DeepMind, Nokia & Index Ventures founders & executives. Bengt Holmstrom, Niklas Zennström, Neil Rimer, Mårten Mickos, Pekka Lundmark & Jussi Westergren! 💙🚀

These 6 PS Fellows are all luminaries in their own way.

Bengt received the Nobel prize for his contributions to contract theory and how organizations design incentives when information is imperfect, a foundation for how modern companies, boards and markets are structured.

Niklas built Skype into Europe’s first unicorn, has ever since invested through Atomico, and has long argued that European founders should build with greater ambition and scale.

Neil co-founded Index Ventures in 1996 and spent over 25 years backing and building companies like Supercell, Betfair, Revolut and Roblox.

Mårten scaled MySQL AB into Europe’s second unicorn by building the backbone of much of the modern web, and spent nearly a decade at HackerOne turning ethical hacking into mainstream security infrastructure.

Pekka led Nokia through its shift to 5G and 6G, and before that served as the CEO of Fortum, Konecranes and Hackman.

Jussi, a theoretical physicist with University of Oxford, was one of Google DeepMind’s founding investors, and has played a key role in founding and advising several companies and philanthropic projects like Academia .edu, Intellectual Ventures, Lateral Logic, G-cluster & Capacity Networks.

What strikes me most is that each of them has built something that outlasted the moment it was built in: a company, a market, a technology, an idea. That is exactly the thinking we need as we build the next generation of European AI.

They join Meredith Whittaker (Signal Technology Foundation & ex-Google & New York University Professor) and Bernhard Schölkopf (ETH Zürich Professor, Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems Director and ELLIS - European Laboratory for Learning and Intelligent Systems founder) as PS Fellows, positions in which these exceptional people take on active roles at PostScriptum companies to drive their success.

Several of us will be on stage at the AI Summit in Turku on 16 November. See you there.

All six, welcome to the team! 💙🚀

posts.description:
Was chatting with Joanna Braunold from my team today about how our brains work in mysterious ways.

The exact moments my mind decides to produce absolute genius, or just figure out the exact next tasks I should actually be working on:
❌ During a 2-hour brainstorming meeting.
❌ Staring blankly at a laptop with a triple espresso.
✔️ 2 minutes into a hot shower with shampoo in my eyes.

The problem? By the time I turn off the water, grab a towel, and find my phone, that insight has evaporated into thin air, leaving me with nothing but a faint scent of lavender and regret.

Forget sending people to Mars, Elon. We need the waterproof Grok Bot Shower Button™️ next to the loofah. Modern problems require wet-fingered solutions.
Let us dictate our shower thoughts before they go down the drain! 🚿💡
(Attached: A preview of the only upgrade my bathroom actually needs 👇, generated by Gemini - I love Agents Collaboration 😊 )
